video_title: Celtics Humble Jaylen Brown | Who’s Really a Contender in the West?

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown's poor performance against the Boston Celtics
quotes.excerpt: This night went about as poorly as it could have for Jaylen Brown.

text_blocks.speaker: Jovan Buha
text_blocks.text: This night went about as poorly as it could have for Jaylen Brown. With the story that came out beforehand and some of the comments he had been making throughout the offseason and early in the season, he was adding fuel to the fire here. For him to have maybe his worst game of the season, just lay a stinker, they have an okay first half, they are hanging around despite not playing their best basketball, they go on this big run to tie the game in the third, and then they just get their ass handed to them the rest of the way.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: Let's tackle Jaylen Brown's individual night to start. I thought he was pressing a little bit, and I think Boston was just very ready for the game. They felt like the more well-coached team, the more well-prepared team. They knew what Philly was going to try to throw at them, but Jaylen Brown's mode of attack would be they crowded him, they crowded his line of sight. They knew that he would be trying to get downhill and that he would be looking to score on those drives, and they kept throwing extra bodies at him, arms, length at him. He had several turnovers, then he is getting offensive fouls, then he is fouling guys in the back. He was just off of his game.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: The tension between Jaylen Brown and the Boston Celtics organization
quotes.excerpt: I could see why Jaylen Brown felt the way because if you are only getting the one side
quotes.quote: I went on Russillo's show and we talked about the Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum situation. Obviously, Ryan is connected to a lot of guys with the Boston Celtics. There is no secret there. He is very well plugged in and connected with the organization. I could tell I threw him off when I was like, well, I could see why Jaylen Brown felt the way because if you are only getting the one side, it is kind of hard to understand how Jaylen Brown could feel like he has ever been slighted by the Celtics. And then, Celtics people made it known to me like, look, there is context to the stuff that Jaylen Brown is saying.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Jayson Tatum's intentional brand of being boring and non-confrontational
quotes.excerpt: I just think some of the non-basketball stuff, he is doing the right thing, but it is boring.

text_blocks.speaker: Jovan Buha
text_blocks.text: It is performative on both sides.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: Yes, it is. It is. For sure. For sure. Tatum is playing his role. I don't make headlines, I don't mix it up in the public, I don't make a spectacle of myself. That is Tatum's MO, for better and for worse, I would say, by the way. I would say that the league would be served by guys making spectacles of themselves and becoming public figures, magnets for attention. That is how you draw eyeballs to your league. I get it, Tatum always gets it done on the court, I am not disputing that, I just think some of the non-basketball stuff, while I get it organizationally and even personally for your own sort of personal peace and not dealing with extra stuff off the court, he is doing the right thing, but it is boring. Tatum is boring. That is his brand. He has cultivated that quite intentionally, right? This is not by accident.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Philadelphia 76ers offensive struggles and team chemistry
quotes.excerpt: I felt the most disjointed the offense looked for a full game.
quotes.quote: Philadelphia, you can still see the growing pains with them. I have watched over half their games at this point and this was I felt the most disjointed the offense looked for a full game. You had LeBron James and Joel Embiid combining to shoot 6 for 21 and I don't think those guys were quite up to par in terms of I mean Joel Embiid drew a ton of fouls to his credit, but he couldn't make a shot. And yeah, I mean Jaylen Brown, he starts the game like face-guarding Jayson Tatum and he is trying to get into him, he is holding him off the ball and stuff and then he kind of eventually eased up on that, but I thought it was telling, you know, single game plus-minus isn't always indicative of a player's performance, but far and away the worst plus-minus on the team, minus 27 in his 26 minutes.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Philadelphia 76ers offensive development and spacing issues
quotes.excerpt: I thought the difference in the game is two offenses in way different forms in terms of their development.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: I thought the difference in the game is two offenses in way different forms in terms of their development from one another. That contrast was stark to me. You got the Celtics who have a machine. They have a system. It is tried and true. It is brought championships, it is gotten to conference finals, it is made Joe Mazzulla coach of the year. It is produced. It has done nothing but produce for three, four years now. And yeah, they plug in Paul George, but this guy is a veteran. This guy is a very high IQ player. The requirements of this offense speak directly to his actual strong suits and skill set. And so you see something seamless happening there, whereas in Philly, it is they have way more to figure out and I thought this game was indicative of that truth.

text_blocks.speaker: Jovan Buha
text_blocks.text: 100% agree. I think you have a team that knows its identity and a team that is still figuring it out. And that to me was the big takeaway on both sides. And I think from the Philly side to in terms of being optimistic, like they have been able to win a ton of games so far while they are still finding themselves and they have had a difficult schedule. They have played the Knicks a couple times, the Pistons a couple times, now the Celtics, the Pacers, so like they have had a really difficult schedule. I know by record the Knicks and the Cavs aren't quite what we expected them to be, but those are still good teams.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Boston Celtics' offensive spacing and defensive challenges
quotes.excerpt: Even when the Jayson Tatum stuff is going, the spacing is clunky.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: To me the Jayson Tatum part is obvious. However, even when the Jayson Tatum stuff is going, the spacing is clunky. You see guys bunched up, they are not disciplined in their spacing principles. I think the secondary stuff has not been clarified yet in terms of, okay, when we are not doing Jayson pick and roll with Joel Embiid or LeBron James up top, what are our secondary actions and who is driving that action? Is it LeBron, is it Joel DHO, is it Jaylen pick and roll? Like they don't, they haven't figured out a pecking order or an order of operations yet. And I think that is going to be very, very key.

text_blocks.speaker: Jovan Buha
text_blocks.text: 100% agree. I think you have a team that knows its identity and a team that is still figuring it out. And that to me was the big takeaway on both sides. And I think from the Philly side to in terms of being optimistic, like they have been able to win a ton of games so far while they are still finding themselves and they have had a difficult schedule. They have played the Knicks a couple times, the Pistons a couple times, now the Celtics, the Pacers, so like they have had a really difficult schedule. I know by record the Knicks and the Cavs aren't quite what we expected them to be, but those are still good teams.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: San Antonio Spurs' recent performance and betting outlook
quotes.excerpt: The Spurs are now 9 and 2, winners of nine straight after a tough start.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: The Spurs are now 9 and 2, winners of nine straight after a tough start. The offense is back. I think they are now up to like number six or something crazy like that, which when they have the type of defense that they have, like come on. They are leading the league in net rating at this point, they are blowing teams out. Victor Wembanyama has just literally been unstoppable. I don't think the big man rotation in Chicago is going to do much to get in the way of that. So yeah, I know it is a crazy number guys, but give me the Spurs on the road against the Bulls.

text_blocks.speaker: Jovan Buha
text_blocks.text: I agree. Right now the Bulls have a 124 defensive rating, which is the worst of all time. This team cannot guard anybody. So I mean yeah, this one might be over in the second quarter. The Spurs are going to completely annihilate them.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Boston Celtics vs. Toronto Raptors betting analysis
quotes.excerpt: The Celtics are a regular season machine.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: The Celtics are a regular season machine. They are blowing teams out. Victor Wembanyama has just literally been unstoppable. I don't think the big man rotation in Chicago is going to do much to get in the way of that. So yeah, I know it is a crazy number guys, but give me the Celtics on the road against the Raptors. They are favored by five and a half points. I get it, that is a huge number for the road team, but the Raptors are still banged up. Scotty Barnes, he might play, but quite frankly, he is coming off of missing time. Kawhi Leonard is still out. Again, the Celtics are a regular season machine.

text_blocks.speaker: Jovan Buha
text_blocks.text: Scotty is out by the way. So yeah, that rolls out. So yeah, I am with you on Boston.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Oklahoma City Thunder vs. Portland Trail Blazers betting analysis
quotes.excerpt: I like this back-to-back, it is not even a home and home, it is just straight.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: I like this back-to-back, it is not even a home and home, it is just straight. Two straight home games in Portland, baseball series game. Thank you. The Trail Blazers kind of wiped the floor with the Thunder in the first game. Damian Lillard had an electric third quarter, made every damn near every single shot to carry the day there. However, I just think again, I think the Trail Blazers would be happy with a split. It is second night of a back-to-back, you never know if Dame even plays, DNP, you know, coaches to rest up type of thing. So yeah, give me the Thunder, who are only favored by a point and a half. So you might as well even go money line there. Give me the Thunder, man. I like them to avenge that embarrassing loss.

text_blocks.speaker: Jovan Buha
text_blocks.text: I thought that game at least through the first like two, two and a half quarters was closer than the final score indicated and then Portland just went off in the third. Dame hit that amazing shot to close the quarter and felt like vintage Dame. But yeah, I think we don't even know if he is playing to your point and uh or maybe they limit his minutes. So I will pick OKC.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Nikola Jokic is a shell of his former offensive self
quotes.excerpt: Nikola Jokic was having the best offensive season in the history of basketball.
quotes.quote: Not only are they finished as contenders, they are done. Nikola Jokic might be done being Nikola Jokic. We have a long sample now since the knee injury that he rushed himself back from last year. Before he went down with that injury, Nikola Jokic was having the best offensive season in NBA history. I repeat, Nikola Jokic was having the best offensive season in the history of basketball. Jordan, Steph, LeBron, Kobe, Shaq, Wilt, you name them. Nikola Jokic was having the best offensive season in the history of basketball. He went down with that injury and he has been a shell of himself.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers defensive rating improves when filtering out garbage time minutes
quotes.excerpt: On cleaning the glass with the filtered out garbage time, they are 13th in defensive rating.
quotes.quote: I think that is all fair. I will give you a couple counterpoints. Per Cleaning the Glass, which filters out garbage time and the Lakers have had some rough garbage time minutes—you throw out Jaden Hardy and Bronny and Cam Reddish and Kevon Looney and some of these lineups—like I don't know if the Toronto game for example, they sub the starters out with two minutes left, they are up by 16. Within a minute and a half, the lead is down to four and that is the Bronny, Hardy, these guys turning the ball over. So that ruins your defensive rating. On Cleaning the Glass with the filtered out garbage time, they are 13th in defensive rating. So still not great, but much better than night. I mean they have been 20th, 21st for most of the season.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers will bounce back despite current injury struggles
quotes.excerpt: I don't think the Clippers are going to maintain a 20% win percentage for 82 games.
quotes.quote: The other teams that have gotten off out the block slow, the Clippers, who have been dealing with injuries and different stuff, I don't think the Clippers are going to maintain a 20% win percentage for 82 games. I think they'll bounce back from this.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Nets have more talent than their record shows
quotes.excerpt: I think the Nets are better than what they've shown and God knows they have more talent.
quotes.quote: Same for the Nets. I think the Nets are better than what they've shown and God knows they have more talent than what they've shown.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Utah Jazz are not a serious team this year
quotes.excerpt: I was told this is a serious team. Vegas had their over-under at 38 wins.
quotes.quote: And then Utah, who again, one in ten. I was told this is a serious team. Vegas had their over-under at 38 wins. We had some breaking news during the show. You see this from Shams: Utah Jazz star Lauri Markkanen has sustained a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month. So no Jaren Jackson, no Lauri Markkanen. The idea this team was going to win 38 games is done. Them taking winning seriously this year is done.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: A.J. Bailey's early season defensive impact
quotes.excerpt: I like what I've seen from A.J. Bailey to start the year.
quotes.quote: They do have a lot of young guys. I like what I've seen from A.J. Bailey to start the year. He's trying his ass off on defense. He's been a nice little transitional kind of player. When the shots are falling, it looks cool.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Darren Peterson's improved comfort level
quotes.excerpt: Darren Peterson, the last three four games, has looked way more comfortable.
quotes.quote: Darren Peterson, the last three four games, has looked way more comfortable. I think they're still trying to figure out who should be the on-ball guy. They are splitting it between him and Keonte George.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Walker Kessler is a better value than Triple J
quotes.excerpt: I would rather have Walker Kessler right now than Triple J, especially factoring in the contract.
quotes.quote: They might have double screwed up with this whole situation in terms of, I would rather have Walker Kessler right now than Triple J, especially factoring in the contract. He's double the rebounder that Triple J is. To say, like even if you want to make the argument that Triple J's defensive ceiling is higher, he's not a center. So you got to have a particular big with him, and then he's always injured. He's making his contracts over 40 million. I would take Kessler's younger, he's making less.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Trading Lauri Markkanen instead of Triple J
quotes.excerpt: What if they would have just got rid of Markkanen and made Triple J the guy?
quotes.quote: That's another idea. It's just like, what if they would have just got rid of Markkanen and made Triple J the guy? I would take Markkanen. I'm not a big Triple J guy.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential of a Kessler, Boozer, Markkanen frontcourt
quotes.excerpt: Imagine if they had a Kessler, Boozer, Markkanen front line.
quotes.quote: Imagine if they had a Kessler, Boozer, Markkanen front line. That to me would be a scary, physically imposing front line, or even Caleb Wilson. I know Wilson was ever really in consideration for number two, it was Boozer, but just the physical traits. Peterson's been like the fourth or fifth best rookie up to this point, maybe fifth if you throw Yaxel in there.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Darren Peterson's lack of elite ball-handling
quotes.excerpt: The problem for me with Peterson, he doesn't have the handle.
quotes.quote: Where I'm a little bit, I disagree with you on Peterson, I think he's got this identifiable elite skill. He's going to put the ball in the hoop and I think he'll one day be very efficient at it. I think the problem for me with Peterson, he doesn't have the handle. I just think he's not a handler. He's not a 24/7 365. He's my point guard. He's the king of my ball-handling duties for this team.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Darren Peterson's defensive potential
quotes.excerpt: If you compare him to say, Trae Young, for example, I think he competes way more.
quotes.quote: He's tiny, but I think if you compare him to say, Trae Young, for example, I think he competes way more on the defensive side than Trae Young. And there's like a physicality with him that Trae Young has never consistently displayed. So I think he will be a defensive liability at the highest level most likely, but I at least like he's got some moxie to him where he'll mix it up and play physically.
